preferences.name: show_empty_coll_nodes
preferences.label: Show empty object collections?
preferences.help_str: If turned off, then all object collections which are empty will be hidden from browser tree.

preferences.name: show_column_datatype
preferences.label: Show column data type?
preferences.help_str: If turned off, then the data types of the columns will not be displayed alongside their column names.

preferences.name: hide_shared_server
preferences.label: Hide shared servers?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, all shared servers will be hidden from the browser tree.

preferences.name: browser_tree_state_save_interval
preferences.label: Object explorer tree state saving interval
preferences.help_str: Object explorer state saving interval in seconds. Use -1 to disable the tree saving mechanism.

preferences.name: confirm_on_refresh_close
preferences.label: Confirm on close or refresh?
preferences.help_str: Confirm that closure or refresh of the browser or browser tab is intended before proceeding.

preferences.name: confirm_on_properties_close
preferences.label: Confirm before Close/Reset in object properties dialog?
preferences.help_str: Confirm before closing or resetting the changes in the properties dialog for an object if the changes are not saved.

preferences.name: auto_expand_sole_children
preferences.label: Auto-expand sole children
preferences.help_str: If a treeview node is expanded and has only a single child, automatically expand the child node as well.

preferences.name: show_server_color_indicator
preferences.label: Show server color indicator in panel tabs?
preferences.help_str: If enabled, a colored circle indicator will be shown in panel tabs (Query Tool, ERD Tool, etc.) matching the server's custom background color.

preferences.name: table_row_count_threshold
preferences.label: Count rows if estimated less than

preferences.name: pgagent_row_threshold
preferences.label: Maximum job history rows
preferences.help_str: The maximum number of history rows to show on the Statistics tab for pgAgent jobs.

preferences.name: process_retain_days
preferences.label: Process details/logs retention days
preferences.help_str: After this many days, the process info and logs will be automatically cleared.

preferences.name: dynamic_tabs
preferences.label: Dynamic tab size
preferences.help_str: If set to True, the tabs will take full size as per the title. This will also apply to already opened tabs.

preferences.name: qt_tab_title_placeholder
preferences.label: Query tool tab title
preferences.help_str: Supported placeholders are %DATABASE%, %USERNAME%, and %SERVER%. Users can provide any string with or without placeholders of their choice. A blank title will revert to the default.

preferences.name: vw_edt_tab_title_placeholder
preferences.label: View/Edit data tab title
preferences.help_str: Supported placeholders are %SCHEMA%, %TABLE%, %DATABASE%, %USERNAME%, and %SERVER%. Users can provide any string with or without placeholders of their choice. A blank title will revert to the default.

preferences.name: debugger_tab_title_placeholder
preferences.label: Debugger tab title
preferences.help_str: Supported placeholders are %FUNCTION%, %ARGS%, %SCHEMA%, and %DATABASE%. Users can provide any string with or without placeholders of their choice. A blank title will revert to the default.

preferences.name: new_browser_tab_open
preferences.label: Open in new browser tab
preferences.help_str: Select Query Tool, Debugger, Schema Diff, ERD Tool, or PSQL Tool from the drop-down to open that module in a new browser tab.

preferences.name: breadcrumbs_enable
preferences.label: Enable object breadcrumbs?
preferences.help_str: Enable breadcrumbs to show the complete path of an object in the object explorer. The breadcrumbs are displayed on object mouse hover.

preferences.name: breadcrumbs_show_comment
preferences.label: Show comment with object breadcrumbs?
preferences.help_str: Show object comment along with breadcrumbs.

preferences.name: plain_editor_mode
preferences.label: Plain text mode?
preferences.help_str: When set to True, keywords won't be highlighted and code folding will be disabled. Plain text mode will improve editor performance with large files.

preferences.name: code_folding
preferences.label: Code folding?
preferences.help_str: Enable or disable code folding. In plain text mode, this will have no effect as code folding is always disabled in that mode. Disabling will improve editor performance with large files.

preferences.name: cursor_blink_rate
preferences.label: Cursor blink rate
preferences.help_str: Adjust the speed at which the text cursor blinks within the editors.

preferences.name: wrap_code
preferences.label: Line wrapping?
preferences.help_str: Specifies whether or not to wrap SQL code in the editor.

preferences.name: insert_pair_brackets
preferences.label: Insert bracket pairs?
preferences.help_str: Specifies whether or not to insert paired brackets in the editor.

preferences.name: highlight_selection_matches
preferences.label: Highlight selection matches?
preferences.help_str: Specifies whether or not to highlight matched selected text in the editor.

preferences.name: brace_matching
preferences.label: Brace matching?
preferences.help_str: Specifies whether or not to highlight matched braces in the editor.

preferences.name: sql_font_size
preferences.label: Font size
preferences.help_str: The font size to use for the SQL text boxes and editors. The value specified is in "em" units, in which 1 is the default relative font size. For example, to increase the font size by 20 percent use a value of 1.2, or to reduce by 20 percent, use a value of 0.8. Minimum 0.1, maximum 10.

preferences.name: sql_font_ligatures
preferences.label: Font ligatures?
preferences.help_str: If set to true, ligatures will be enabled in SQL text boxes and editors provided the configured font family supports them.

preferences.name: sql_font_family
preferences.label: Font family
preferences.help_str: Specify the font family to be used for all SQL editors. The specified font should already be installed on your system. If the font is not found, the editor will fall back to the default font, Source Code Pro.

preferences.name: indent_new_line
preferences.label: Auto-indent new line?
preferences.help_str: Specifies whether the newly added line using enter key should be auto-indented or not

preferences.name: keyword_case
preferences.label: Keyword case
preferences.help_str: Convert keywords to upper, lower, or preserve casing.

preferences.name: identifier_case
preferences.label: Identifier case
preferences.help_str: Convert identifiers to upper, lower, or preserve casing.

preferences.name: function_case
preferences.label: Function case
preferences.help_str: Convert function names to upper, lower, or preserve casing.

preferences.name: data_type_case
preferences.label: Data type case
preferences.help_str: Convert data types to upper, lower, or preserve casing.

preferences.name: spaces_around_operators
preferences.label: Spaces around operators?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, spaces are used around all operators.

preferences.name: tab_size
preferences.label: Tab size
preferences.help_str: The number of spaces per tab. Minimum 2, maximum 8.

preferences.name: use_spaces
preferences.label: Use spaces?
preferences.help_str: Specifies whether or not to insert spaces instead of tabs when the tab key or auto-indent are used.

preferences.name: expression_width
preferences.label: Expression Width
preferences.help_str: Maximum number of characters in parenthesized expressions to be kept on a single line.

preferences.name: logical_operator_new_line
preferences.label: Logical operator new line
preferences.help_str: Decides newline placement before or after logical operators (AND, OR, XOR).

preferences.name: lines_between_queries
preferences.label: Lines between queries
preferences.help_str: Decides how many empty lines to leave between SQL statements. A value of zero means no empty lines are added.

preferences.name: new_line_before_semicolon
preferences.label: New line before semicolon?
preferences.help_str: Whether to place query separator (;) on a separate line.

preferences.label: PostgreSQL Help Path
preferences.help_str: Path to the PostgreSQL documentation. $VERSION$ will be replaced with the major.minor version number.

preferences.name: session_stats_refresh
preferences.label: Session statistics refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.name: tps_stats_refresh
preferences.label: Transaction throughput refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.name: ti_stats_refresh
preferences.label: Tuples in refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.name: to_stats_refresh
preferences.label: Tuples out refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.name: bio_stats_refresh
preferences.label: Block I/O statistics refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.name: hpc_stats_refresh
preferences.label: Handle & Process count statistics refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.name: cpu_stats_refresh
preferences.label: CPU usage by process mode refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.name: la_stats_refresh
preferences.label: Average load statistics refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.name: pcpu_stats_refresh
preferences.label: CPU usage per process statistics refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.name: m_stats_refresh
preferences.label: Memory usage statistics refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.label: Swap memory usage statistics refresh rate

preferences.name: pmu_stats_refresh
preferences.label: Memory usage per process statistics refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.name: io_stats_refresh
preferences.label: I/O analysis statistics refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.name: pgd_replication_lag_refresh
preferences.label: PGD replication lag refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between graph samples.

preferences.name: show_graphs
preferences.label: Show activity?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, activity will be displayed on dashboards.

preferences.name: show_activity
preferences.label: Show state?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, state tables will be displayed on dashboards.

preferences.name: long_running_query_threshold
preferences.label: Long running query thresholds
preferences.help_str: Set the warning and alert threshold value to highlight the long-running queries on the dashboard.

preferences.name: graph_data_points
preferences.label: Show graph data points?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, data points will be visible on graph lines.

preferences.name: use_diff_point_style
preferences.label: Use different data point styles?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, data points will be visible in a different style on each graph line.

preferences.name: graph_mouse_track
preferences.label: Show mouse hover tooltip?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, a tooltip will appear on mouse hover on the graph lines showing the data point details.

preferences.name: graph_line_border_width
preferences.label: Chart line width
preferences.help_str: Set the width of the lines on the line chart.

preferences.name: default_provider
preferences.label: Default Provider
preferences.help_str: The LLM provider to use for AI features. Select "None (Disabled)" to disable AI features. Note: AI features must also be enabled in the server configuration (LLM_ENABLED) for this setting to take effect.

preferences.name: max_tool_iterations
preferences.label: Max Tool Iterations
preferences.help_str: Maximum number of tool call iterations allowed during an AI conversation. Higher values allow more complex queries but may consume more resources. Default is 20.

preferences.name: anthropic_api_url
preferences.label: API URL
preferences.help_str: URL for the Anthropic API endpoint. Leave empty to use the default (https://api.anthropic.com/v1). Set a custom URL to use an Anthropic-compatible API provider.

preferences.name: anthropic_api_key_file
preferences.label: API Key File
preferences.help_str: Path to a file containing your Anthropic API key. This path must be on the server hosting pgAdmin, e.g. inside the container when using Docker. The file should contain only the API key. The API key may be optional when using a custom API URL with a provider that does not require authentication.

preferences.name: anthropic_api_model
preferences.label: Model
preferences.help_str: The Anthropic model to use. Models are loaded dynamically from your API key. You can also type a custom model name. Leave empty to use the default (Claude Sonnet 4).

control_props.placeholder: Select or type a model name...

preferences.name: openai_api_url
preferences.label: API URL
preferences.help_str: URL for the OpenAI API endpoint. Leave empty to use the default (https://api.openai.com/v1). Set a custom URL to use any OpenAI-compatible API provider such as LiteLLM, LM Studio, or EXO. The URL should include the /v1 path prefix if required by your provider (e.g., http://localhost:1234/v1).

preferences.name: openai_api_key_file
preferences.label: API Key File
preferences.help_str: Path to a file containing your OpenAI API key. This path must be on the server hosting pgAdmin, e.g. inside the container when using Docker. The file should contain only the API key. The API key may be optional when using a custom API URL with a provider that does not require authentication.

preferences.name: openai_api_model
preferences.label: Model
preferences.help_str: The OpenAI model to use. Models are loaded dynamically from your API key. You can also type a custom model name. Leave empty to use the default (GPT-4o).

control_props.placeholder: Select or type a model name...

preferences.name: ollama_api_url
preferences.label: API URL
preferences.help_str: URL for the Ollama API endpoint (e.g., http://localhost:11434).

preferences.name: ollama_api_model
preferences.label: Model
preferences.help_str: The Ollama model to use. Models are loaded dynamically from your Ollama server. You can also type a custom model name. Leave empty to use the default (llama3.2).

control_props.placeholder: Select or type a model name...

preferences.name: docker_api_url
preferences.label: API URL
preferences.help_str: URL for the Docker Model Runner API endpoint (e.g., http://localhost:12434). Available in Docker Desktop 4.40 and later. Tip: You can also use the OpenAI provider with a custom API URL for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including Docker Model Runner.

preferences.name: docker_api_model
preferences.label: Model
preferences.help_str: The Docker model to use. Models are loaded dynamically from your Docker Model Runner. You can also type a custom model name. Leave empty to use the default (ai/qwen3-coder).

control_props.placeholder: Select or type a model name...

preferences.name: theme
preferences.label: Theme
preferences.help_str: Click the save button to apply the theme. Below is the preview of the theme.

preferences.name: layout
preferences.label: Layout
preferences.help_str: Choose the layout that suits you best. pgAdmin offers two options: the Classic layout, a longstanding and familiar design, and the Workspace layout, which provides distraction free dedicated areas for the Query Tool, PSQL, and Schema Diff tools.

preferences.name: open_in_res_workspace
preferences.label: Open the Query Tool/PSQL in their respective workspaces
preferences.help_str: This setting applies only when the layout is set to Workspace Layout. When set to True, all Query Tool/PSQL tabs will open in their respective workspaces. By default, this setting is False, meaning that Query Tool/PSQL tabs will open in the currently active workspace (either the default or the workspace selected at the time of opening)

preferences.name: save_app_state
preferences.label: Save the application state?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, pgAdmin will save the state of opened tools (such as Query Tool, PSQL, Schema Diff, and ERD), including any unsaved data. This data will be automatically restored in the event of an unexpected shutdown or browser refresh.

preferences.name: enable_binary_data_download
preferences.label: Enable binary data download?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, binary data can be downloaded from the result grid. The default is False to prevent excessive memory usage on the server.

preferences.name: sql_with_drop
preferences.label: SQL With DROP Table
preferences.help_str: If enabled, the SQL generated by the ERD Tool will add DROP table DDL before each CREATE table DDL.

preferences.name: table_relation_depth
preferences.label: Table Relation Depth
preferences.help_str: The maximum depth pgAdmin should traverse to find related tables when generating an ERD for a table. Use -1 for no limit.

preferences.name: insert_table_with_relations
preferences.label: Insert Table With Relations
preferences.help_str: Whether inserting a table via drag and drop should also insert its relations to the existing tables in the diagram.

preferences.name: cardinality_notation
preferences.label: Cardinality Notation
preferences.help_str: Notation to be used to present cardinality.

preferences.name: image_pixel_ratio
preferences.label: Image Download Resolution
preferences.help_str: Higher values will use higher memory and slower rendering.

preferences.name: format_pgerd
preferences.label: Format ERD Project File?
preferences.help_str: If enabled, the .pgerd project file of the ERD tool will be formatted before saving.

preferences.name: ignore_whitespaces
preferences.label: Ignore Whitespace
preferences.help_str: Set ignore whitespace on or off by default in the drop-down menu near the Compare button in the Schema Diff tab.

preferences.name: ignore_owner
preferences.label: Ignore Owner
preferences.help_str: Set ignore owner on or off by default in the drop-down menu near the Compare button in the Schema Diff tab.

preferences.name: ignore_tablespace
preferences.label: Ignore Tablespace
preferences.help_str: Set ignore tablespace on or off by default in the drop-down menu near the Compare button in the Schema Diff tab.

preferences.name: ignore_grants
preferences.label: Ignore Grants/Revoke
preferences.help_str: Set ignore grants/revoke on or off by default in the drop-down menu near the Compare button in the Schema Diff tab.

preferences.name: auto_commit
preferences.label: Auto commit?
preferences.help_str: Set auto commit on or off by default in new Query Tool tabs.

preferences.name: auto_rollback
preferences.label: Auto rollback on error?
preferences.help_str: Set auto rollback on or off by default in new Query Tool tabs.

preferences.name: server_cursor
preferences.label: Use server cursor?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, the dataset will be fetched using a server-side cursor after the query is executed. This allows controlled data transfer to the client, enabling examination of large datasets without loading them entirely into memory.

preferences.name: prompt_save_query_changes
preferences.label: Prompt to save unsaved query changes?
preferences.help_str: Specifies whether or not to prompt the user to save unsaved queries on Query Tool exit.

preferences.name: table_view_data_by_pk
preferences.label: Sort View Data results by primary key columns?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, data returned when using the View/Edit Data - All Rows option will be sorted by the Primary Key columns by default. When using the First/Last 100 Rows options, data is always sorted.

preferences.name: view_data_default_row_limit
preferences.label: Default row limit for View Data
preferences.help_str: Specify the maximum number of rows to fetch when using the View/Edit Data - All Rows option. This appends a LIMIT clause to the generated query, which can significantly improve performance on very large tables. Set to 0 (the default) to fetch all rows with no limit (the existing behavior). This does not affect the First/Last 100 Rows options.

preferences.name: prompt_save_data_changes
preferences.label: Prompt to save unsaved data changes?
preferences.help_str: Specifies whether or not to prompt the user to save unsaved data on data grid exit.

preferences.name: prompt_commit_transaction
preferences.label: Prompt to commit/rollback active transactions?
preferences.help_str: Specifies whether or not to prompt the user to commit or rollback an active transaction on Query Tool exit.

preferences.name: copy_sql_to_query_tool
preferences.label: Copy SQL from main window to query tool?
preferences.help_str: Specifies whether or not to copy SQL to the Query Tool from the main window.

preferences.name: open_in_new_tab
preferences.label: Open the file in a new tab?
preferences.help_str: Specifies whether or not to open the file in a new tab.

preferences.name: view_edit_promotion_warning
preferences.label: Show View/Edit Data Promotion Warning?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, the View/Edit Data tool will show a confirmation dialog to promote to Query Tool when the query is edited.

preferences.name: underline_query_cursor
preferences.label: Underline query at cursor?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, the Query Tool will parse and underline the query at the cursor position.

preferences.name: underlined_query_execute_warning
preferences.label: Underlined query execute warning?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, the Query Tool will display a warning when clicking the Execute Query button. The warning will appear only if "Underline query at cursor?" is set to False.

preferences.name: csv_replace_nulls_with
preferences.label: Replace null values with
preferences.help_str: Specifies the string that represents a null value while downloading query results as CSV. You can specify any arbitrary string to represent a null value, with quotes if desired.

preferences.name: results_grid_quote_char
preferences.label: Result copy quote character. Not applied when copying a single cell.

preferences.name: column_data_auto_resize
preferences.label: Columns sized by
preferences.help_str: If set to 'Column data', columns will auto-size to the maximum width of the data in the column as loaded in the first batch. If set to 'Column name', the column will be sized to the widest of the data type or column name.

preferences.name: column_data_max_width
preferences.label: Maximum column width
preferences.help_str: Specify the maximum width of the column in pixels when 'Columns sized by' is set to 'Column data'.

preferences.name: data_result_rows_per_page
preferences.label: Data result rows per page
preferences.help_str: Specify the number of records to fetch in one batch. Changing this value will override the DATA_RESULT_ROWS_PER_PAGE setting from the config file.

preferences.name: striped_rows
preferences.label: Striped rows?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, the result grid will display rows with alternating background colors.

preferences.name: max_column_data_display_length
preferences.label: Max column data display length
preferences.help_str: Maximum number of characters to display in a data cell.

preferences.name: connection_status
preferences.label: Connection status
preferences.help_str: If set to True, the Query Tool will monitor and display the connection and transaction status.

preferences.name: connection_status_fetch_time
preferences.label: Connection status refresh rate
preferences.help_str: The number of seconds between connection/transaction status polls.

preferences.name: query_success_notification
preferences.label: Show query success notification?
preferences.help_str: If set to True, the Query Tool will show notifications on successful query execution.

preferences.name: keywords_in_uppercase
preferences.label: Keywords in uppercase
preferences.help_str: If set to True, keywords will be displayed in upper case for autocomplete.

preferences.name: autocomplete_on_key_press
preferences.label: Autocomplete on key press
preferences.help_str: If set to True, autocomplete will be available on key press along with CTRL/CMD + Space. If set to False, autocomplete is only activated when CTRL/CMD + Space is pressed.

preferences.name: row_limit
preferences.label: Row Limit
preferences.help_str: This setting specifies the maximum number of rows that will be plotted on a chart. Increasing this limit may impact performance if charts are plotted with very high numbers of rows.

preferences.name: custom_tile_url
preferences.label: Custom tile provider URL
preferences.help_str: URL template of a custom XYZ tile provider used as a base layer in the Geometry Viewer, e.g. https://myserver.example.com/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png. The template must contain the {x}, {y} and {z} placeholders, and may contain {s} for subdomains (a, b, c). Leave empty to disable the custom tile provider. Defaults to the administrator-configured DEFAULT_GEOMETRY_VIEWER_PROVIDER, if any.

preferences.name: custom_tile_name
preferences.label: Custom tile provider name
preferences.help_str: Display name of the custom tile provider in the layer selector of the Geometry Viewer.

preferences.name: custom_tile_crs
preferences.label: Custom tile provider CRS
preferences.help_str: Coordinate reference system of the custom tile provider. If it is not EPSG:3857 (Web Mercator), the built-in tile layers will be hidden as they cannot be mixed with other coordinate systems.

preferences.name: custom_tile_attribution
preferences.label: Custom tile provider attribution
preferences.help_str: Attribution text shown on the map for the custom tile provider. May contain HTML links.

preferences.name: custom_tile_max_zoom
preferences.label: Custom tile provider max zoom
preferences.help_str: Maximum zoom level of the custom tile provider.
